findings.source_passage: a long, limber, portentous, black mass of something hovering in the centre of the picture over three blue, dim, perpendicular lines floating in a nameless yeast. A boggy, soggy, squitchy picture truly
findings.source_locator: second paragraph of the oilpainting description
findings.why_it_matters: This is the central ekphrastic set-piece of the chapter — 'boggy, soggy, squitchy' is one of Melville's most celebrated sonic passages and critics return to it constantly; the entire paragraph introducing the 'portentous black mass' is the lead-up to the leviathan identification and is absent from the draft.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full paragraph beginning 'But what most puzzled and confounded you was a long, limber, portentous, black mass' through 'A boggy, soggy, squitchy picture truly, enough to drive a nervous man distracted' — at minimum the 'boggy, soggy, squitchy' phrase must survive verbatim.

findings.source_passage: in the time of the New England hags, had endeavored to delineate chaos bewitched. But by dint of much and earnest contemplation, and oft repeated ponderings
findings.why_it_matters: The 'New England hags' reference and the mock-scholarly 'by dint of much and earnest contemplation' are voice-defining ironies establishing Ishmael's register; their erasure flattens the narrator's characteristic mock-solemnity.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'in the time of the New England hags' and the 'by dint of much and earnest contemplation' clause to preserve Ishmael's ironic scholarly pose.

findings.source_passage: The original iron entered nigh the tail, and, like a restless needle sojourning in the body of a man, travelled full forty feet, and at last was found imbedded in the hump.
findings.why_it_matters: The simile 'like a restless needle sojourning in the body of a man' is distinctively Melvillean and carries thematic weight about obsession and the whale's body; the draft retains only Nathan Swain and drops the iron entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the iron/corkscrew harpoon detail with the 'restless needle' simile after the Nathan Swain sentence.

findings.source_passage: You shuddered as you gazed, and wondered what monstrous cannibal and savage could ever have gone a death-harvesting with such a hacking, horrifying implement.
findings.source_locator: weapons-wall paragraph, clubs and spears description
findings.why_it_matters: The 'death-harvesting' formulation and the rhetorical address ('you shuddered') are voice-establishing; the detailed description of hair-tufted clubs and the sickle-shaped weapon is entirely cut, erasing the cannibal-threat motif that recurs through the chapter.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore at least one sentence on the 'heathenish' clubs — the 'death-harvesting' phrase or the sickle weapon description — to maintain the motif.

findings.source_passage: I now took the measure of the bench, and found that it was a foot too short; but that could be mended with a chair. But it was a foot too narrow... a series of small whirlwinds in the immediate vicinity
findings.source_locator: bench-measuring comedy sequence, after the planing scene
findings.why_it_matters: The bench-measurement farce is a signature comic set-piece demonstrating Ishmael's self-defeating rationalism; the whole sequence of failed solutions (too short, too narrow, two-bench misalignment, cold drafts) enacts the chapter's comedy of discomfort and is entirely cut.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore at least the gist of the bench-measuring failure sequence, including the whirlwinds from the two currents — the comic futility is essential voice material.

findings.source_passage: I never saw such a sight in my life. I tore myself out of it in such a hurry that I gave myself a kink in the neck.
findings.why_it_matters: Ishmael's physical comedy trying on the poncho before a mirror is a signature moment of self-deprecating humour that establishes his character; both the mirror scene and the 'kink in the neck' punchline are absent.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the mirror scene: 'I went up in it to a bit of glass stuck against the wall, and I never saw such a sight in my life. I tore myself out of it in such a hurry that I gave myself a kink in the neck.'

findings.source_passage: the man's a human being just as I am: he has just as much reason to fear me, as I have to be afraid of him. Better sleep with a sober cannibal than a drunken Christian.
findings.why_it_matters: The 'just as much reason to fear me' clause is the interpretive turning point — Ishmael recognises mutual vulnerability, not mere tolerance — and the full moral logic depends on it; the draft preserves only 'the man's a human being' and the 'sober cannibal' line, losing the reciprocity that critics read as the novel's racial-ethical keynote.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'he has just as much reason to fear me, as I have to be afraid of him' before the 'Better sleep' line.

findings.source_passage: his very legs were marked, as if a parcel of dark green frogs were running up the trunks of young palms.
findings.why_it_matters: This simile is one of Melville's most striking image-coinages in the chapter and exemplifies his characteristic exotic naturalism; its loss flattens the ekphrasis of Queequeg's tattoos.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the 'dark green frogs running up the trunks of young palms' simile in the tattooing description.

findings.source_passage: Sal and me slept in that ere bed the night we were spliced. There's plenty of room for two to kick about in that bed... Sam got pitched on the floor, and came near breaking his arm. Arter that, Sal said it wouldn't do.
findings.why_it_matters: The landlord's Sal-and-Sam anecdote is a minor but characteristic comic digression establishing Peter Coffin's voice and the inn's human texture; its absence contributes to voice flattening of the landlord character.
findings.suggested_fix: Consider restoring one sentence of the Sal/Sam story to maintain the landlord's comic garrulousness.

summary: The draft commits a high-severity erasure of the 'long, limber, portentous, black mass / boggy, soggy, squitchy' ekphrastic paragraph — the chapter's most celebrated prose passage — plus a high-severity voice erasure of the 'New England hags' / mock-scholarly irony, and accumulates five medium-severity losses including the bench-measuring farce, the 'restless needle' harpoon simile, the poncho mirror comedy, the 'dark green frogs' tattoo simile, and the reciprocity clause ('just as much reason to fear me') that is the interpretive crux of the Ishmael-Queequeg resolution.
